description:
## What

`pkix_chain::verify_chain(&[Certificate], &[TrustAnchor], now, &Verifier, &RevChecker) -> Result<ValidatedPath, Error>` is per-chain shaped. Setup cost is light (no fork+exec; trust anchor parsing happens once if anchors are reused). Question: does the workspace need a batch entry point like `verify_chains(&[&[Certificate]], &[TrustAnchor], ...) -> Vec<Result<ValidatedPath, Error>>`?

## Options

- **A) No batch entry point.** Callers loop over verify_chain themselves. Setup is light; the loop is fine. Matches current state.

- **B) Add verify_chains batch entry point.** Amortizes any shared state (caching the SignatureVerifier's algorithm dispatch table, caching trust anchor parsing, etc.). Marginal performance gain but explicit batch shape signals support.

- **C) Add a Verifier struct that holds prepared state.** Bigger API change: `let v = Verifier::new(anchors, &sig_verifier, &rev_checker); v.verify_one(chain) / v.verify_batch(&[chain])`. This is closer to mozilla::pkix's TrustDomain shape. Better caching story (anchor pre-processing happens once). Bigger surface change.

## Considerations

- AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 explicitly singles out adapter crates with subprocess overhead as needing batch (1000x asymptotic cost penalty without it). verify_chain has no subprocess; the asymptotic argument is much weaker.
- Real-world batch use cases (CT log scan, enterprise audit) tend to want adapter-style processing anyway: zlint findings, OCSP checks, etc. — those are where batch matters more.
- Callers can wrap verify_chain in a Rayon parallel iterator today without any workspace API change. That's basically a batch entry point at the caller layer.

## Tentative position

A (no batch entry point) is probably right unless someone surfaces a concrete cost benefit. Setup is light; caller-side wrapping is trivial. The asymptotic case in #6 was specifically about subprocess overhead in adapter crates. verify_chain isn't that.

## Out of scope

- Implementing options B or C
- Designing a Verifier struct shape

## Decision-gate

Human label. Surface when there's a concrete consumer or measurement driving the question — until then, A by default.
title: Decide whether verify_chain needs a batch entry point
